source.description: Project parser/check point where the attacker-controlled proxy string is parsed; parse failure enters the vulnerable cleanup path.

sink.description: Second free of c->header_buf, which aliases the already-freed buf pointer.

root_cause.description: On proxy_parse failure, buf is freed directly even though ownership has already been stored in c->header_buf and will be released by flb_http_client_destroy(c).

taint_source.description: The fuzz harness passes a PoC-derived proxy string into flb_http_client(); fluent-bit parses that string here.

tainted_value_origin.description: A malformed attacker-controlled proxy value makes proxy_parse return non-zero, selecting the vulnerable cleanup branch.

coarse_trace.summary: The HTTP header buffer is allocated and assigned to c->header_buf.
The attacker-controlled proxy string is parsed; malformed input drives the error branch.
The error branch frees buf directly even though c owns it through c->header_buf.
Destroying c frees c->header_buf, producing the double-free.

fine_trace.note: Project parser consumes the attacker-controlled proxy string; malformed proxy syntax produces ret != 0. The buffer ownership state in the next steps was established earlier in the same flb_http_client call before this parser branch.

grounding.evidence: Step is in the same sanitizer crash-stack function within a small source-line drift window.

fine_trace.note: ASan allocation context: the header buffer that will later be freed twice is allocated in the same flb_http_client invocation before proxy parsing.
Ownership of buf is stored in the HTTP client object; from this point destroy(c) is responsible for freeing it.

grounding.evidence: No sanitizer or patch artifact directly grounded this step.

fine_trace.note: The branch is entered only when the attacker-controlled proxy argument is present.

grounding.evidence: Step is in the same sanitizer crash-stack function within a small source-line drift window.

fine_trace.note: The parse failure selects the cleanup path that contains the ownership bug.

grounding.evidence: Step is in the same sanitizer crash-stack function within a small source-line drift window.

fine_trace.note: Root cause: premature direct free of buf while c->header_buf still aliases the same allocation and remains scheduled for destruction.

grounding.evidence: Step is in the same sanitizer crash-stack function within a small source-line drift window.
Step is on a changed patch line or a patch hunk line with a patch-groundable role.

fine_trace.note: The same error path immediately destroys c after the premature free.

grounding.evidence: Step file/line appears in sanitizer crash_stack.

fine_trace.note: ASan crash location: c->header_buf still equals buf, so this is the second free of the same allocation.

grounding.evidence: Step file/line appears in sanitizer crash_stack.

root_cause_analysis.summary: flb_http_client() allocates a request header buffer and stores it in c->header_buf. When an attacker-controlled proxy string is present, proxy_parse(proxy, c) parses it. If the proxy string is malformed, the error branch first calls flb_free(buf) and then calls flb_http_client_destroy(c). Because c->header_buf still aliases buf, the destructor frees c->header_buf again, triggering a heap double-free.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch removes the direct flb_free(buf) from the proxy_parse error branch. Since c owns the buffer through c->header_buf, flb_http_client_destroy(c) remains the single cleanup path and releases the buffer exactly once.
